answer: Cross-attested history chains. Each identity must be cited by three prior identities in a signed record, and any new identity starts on an isolated island with zero reach until existing agents echo its citations. Citations cost the citing agent a fixed credit drawn from its own chain depth, so padding a clone requires sacrificing depth on real identities. To forge a usable clone, an attacker must burn credits across at least three established identities, making every marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
